Needs changes before merge.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The PR changes posted G-code.

The registry entries, machine parser checks, and named refusals have passing tests. No UI files change. No dependency or process files change in this PR.

### Requested before merge

1. **[P1] Correct the probe contact check** — `assets/posts/hurco-winmax.cps:923`. The recorded probe program emits `IF[ABS[#5061-38]GE0.001]GOTO9001` before its no-contact alarm. A correct touch at X=38 falls into the alarm. A no-contact endpoint at X=43 passes this check. The opposite endpoint at X=17 also passes. Their mean is 30, so the later deviation check passes with no contact. The same error affects Y. I posted the recorded probe stream locally: it produced this program with no warnings. Use the documented skip-status variable to distinguish contact from no contact. Check unexpected contact on GUARD moves too. Add tests for correct contact, no contact, unexpected contact, and inch output. Update the probe golden after these checks pass. Hurco documents `#3020` as the contact status of the G31 move. [Hurco NCPP variable summary](https://support.hurco.com/wp-content/uploads/hurco_mill/NC_Programming/NCPP_Variable_Summary.htm).

2. **[P2] Use the documented WinMax work-offset variables** — `assets/posts/hurco-winmax.cps:986`. The script calculates a Fanuc-style base of `5201 + wcsIndex * 20`. The probe golden therefore writes `G10 L2 P2 X[#5221+#190] Y[#5222+#191]`. Hurco documents X offsets in `#2501..#2599`, Y offsets in `#2601..#2699`, and Z offsets in `#2701..#2799`. The published table does not define `#5221` or `#5222`. Use the WinMax variables for the active source offset. Test a nonzero source offset, a different target offset, and an auxiliary source offset. Correct the golden. The G/M-word allowlist does not validate these macro variable numbers. [Hurco NCPP variable summary](https://support.hurco.com/wp-content/uploads/hurco_mill/NC_Programming/NCPP_Variable_Summary.htm).

3. **[P2] Supply the required simulator evidence** — `docs/decisions/2573-hurco-winmax-post.md:50`. Issue #2573 requires one short program per open dialect question in the owner's WinMax simulator. It requires the load result and the comparison with the CamCraft path on the issue. The PR and decision file explicitly state that these checks did not run. Record those results before marking the issue complete. [Issue #2573](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/2573).

### Local validation

Trial merge with upstream/main `1ae4d061f20a4b6721d202727dd67f89dddf9e35` succeeded. I used `.claude/worktrees/review-2646`. No GitHub runner ran.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --no-run -j 6`: passed.
- Post suites: `hurco_winmax_post` 8, `script_hurco_winmax` 11, `bore_cycle` 9, `comp_plane` 3, `decimal_point_fanuc_family` 3, `declared_options` 3, `end_units` 3, `first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family` 9, `radius_arcs` 7 passed.
- App suites: `hurco_winmax_post` 2, `conformance` 7, `machine` 33, `machine_library` 11, `post_spindle_rule_all` 5 passed.
- Total: 114 tests passed; none failed or ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -j 6 -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Independent mutation: removed the O-number guard. `extended_work_offsets_and_safe_retract_and_o_word` failed on O10000. Restored the guard: passed.
- Independent mutation: disabled the `rigidTapping === false` guard. `tapping_modes_and_rigid_tapping_guard` failed. Restored the guard: passed.
- I read all 21 new NC goldens line by line and the four refusal goldens. No existing golden changed. The probe golden contains the defects above.

The quick-plan dry run selected unrelated upstream changes through the old merge base. I ran the touched suites directly instead. These tests do not execute the NC macros on a WinMax control. No physical machine or WinMax simulator ran.

Nonblocking note: remove the old statements that this replacement PR is stacked on #2506. They contradict the opening paragraph.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed:

- Finding 1: Each TOUCH requires `#3020=1`. Each GUARD requires `#3020=0`. `contact_status_checks_every_touch_and_guard_in_mm_and_inch` pins contact, no contact, unexpected contact, and inch output. The old contact implementation fails this pin. The restored fix passes.
- Finding 2: Source offsets use the documented WinMax axis registers. `probe_offsets_use_active_winmax_source_and_independent_target` pins nonzero standard offsets, separate targets, auxiliary offsets, and default G54. The old register calculation fails this pin. The restored fix passes.
- Updated the probe golden after the semantic tests passed. Final Hurco suites: 21 passed. Clippy for `camcraft-post` and `camcraft-app`: passed.
- Removed the stale statements that this PR is stacked on #2506.

Finding 3 remains open. No WinMax simulator interface or results are available in this session. The decision file states that simulator verification remains pending. Issue #2573 remains incomplete.

Quick gate: RED, 647 steps, one failure. `continuous_4axis_part::the_continuous_4axis_part_posts_its_wrapped_program` reports a stale example: `/version: 71 != 70`. The same failure occurs with the original reviewed post restored. No unrelated fixture changed.

Please re-review this head. The PR remains a draft.

Needs changes before merge.

This is a SAFETY-tier review because the PR changes posted G-code.

Earlier findings 1 and 2 are met. Each TOUCH and GUARD checks `#3020`. Source offsets use the documented WinMax axis registers. The new tests cover contact status, inch output, standard offsets, auxiliary offsets, and separate targets. The probe golden matches these changes. The [Hurco variable table](https://support.hurco.com/wp-content/uploads/hurco_mill/NC_Programming/NCPP_Variable_Summary.htm) supports these choices.

### Requested before merge

1. **[P1] Seat a cycle at the stated hop before movement between holes** — `assets/posts/hurco-winmax.cps:810`. After the first traverse, `xyFirst()` returns without checking the next hole. `onCycle()` then writes another cycle at the current R level. I used the existing `cycle_hop.rs::back_to_back()` input construction with the Hurco post. The CLI returned success without warnings and wrote:

   ```gcode
   G00 X10. Y10. Z1.
   G99 G73 X10. Y10. Z-20. Q4. R1. F60
   G99 G73 X30. Y10. Z-15. Q4. R1. F60
   ```

   The stream states `RetractPlane 3`, but movement to X30 occurs at Z1. This can hit material between the holes. Removing `RetractPlane` also returns success. [Hurco documents G99 return to R between locations](https://support.hurco.com/wp-content/uploads/hurco_mill/NC_Programming/Canned_Cycle_Descriptions.htm). Cancel the cycle before movement to another hole. Raise to the section's hop, traverse, then descend to R. Refuse the move when the required hop is absent. Add Hurco to `cycle_hop.rs` coverage, including back-to-back cycles and cycles after probing.

2. **[P2] Supply the required simulator evidence** — `docs/decisions/2573-hurco-winmax-post.md:63`. Earlier finding 3 remains open. [Issue #2573](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/2573) requires short programs checked in the owner's WinMax simulator. Record each load result and path comparison on the issue. The PR still ends with `Fixes #2573`, although its body and decision file say these checks remain pending. Local tests do not meet this acceptance requirement.

3. **[P3] Use the required vendor value for a new post** — `assets/posts/hurco-winmax.cps:7`. Set `vendor = "Camcraft"`. Current upstream `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` explicitly requires this value for new files.

### Local validation

The trial merge with upstream/main `136f19763e791b397eb7b2609247230ac1007363` succeeded. All builds and tests ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-2646`. No GitHub runner ran. I used current upstream main's project laws.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --no-run -j 6`: passed.
- Post suites passed: `hurco_winmax_post` 8, `hurco_winmax_probe` 2, `script_hurco_winmax` 11, `bore_cycle` 9, `comp_plane` 3, `decimal_point_fanuc_family` 3, `declared_options` 3, `end_units` 3, `first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family` 9, `radius_arcs` 7.
- App suites passed: `hurco_winmax_post` 2, `conformance` 7, `machine` 33, `machine_library` 11, `post_spindle_rule_all` 5.
- Total: 116 passed; none failed or ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -j 6 -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Independent contact mutation: changed the TOUCH success condition from `#3020EQ1` to `#3020EQ0`. `contact_status_checks_every_touch_and_guard_in_mm_and_inch` failed. Restored condition: passed.
- Independent offset mutation: restored the old Fanuc register calculation and axis stride. `probe_offsets_use_active_winmax_source_and_independent_target` failed on register 5221 instead of 2501. Restored calculation: passed.
- I restored both mutations without a code change. I read all 21 NC goldens and four refusal goldens line by line. No existing golden changes.
- The quick-plan dry run selected 894 steps, including unrelated upstream changes through the old merge base. I ran the touched suites directly. I did not run the full quick gate or reproduce its reported example-version failure.

No UI, dependency, or process files change in this PR. No WinMax simulator or physical machine ran. The passing suites do not include Hurco in the cycle-hop matrix; the CLI reproduction above exposes that gap.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed:

- Finding 1: Cancel the cycle before travel to another hole. Raise to the section hop, traverse, then descend to R. Refuse missing hops. Pins: `back_to_back_cycle_records_traverse_at_the_hop`, `back_to_back_cycle_records_without_a_hop_are_refused_by_name`, `a_cycle_read_after_probing_or_cutting_is_seated_at_the_hop`, and `a_cycle_read_after_probing_without_a_hop_is_refused_by_name`. Removing cycle seating fails four pins. Removing feed tracking or arc tracking also fails the approach pin. Restored fixes pass. The synthesized Hurco golden includes the safe hops.
- Finding 3: Set `vendor = "Camcraft"`. Pin: `hurco_post_vendor_is_camcraft`. Restoring `Hurco` fails the pin. Restoring `Camcraft` passes.

Finding 2 remains open. No WinMax simulator access, load results, or path comparisons are available here or on issue #2573. The decision file records this limit. The PR now uses `Refs #2573`. The issue remains incomplete.

Validation: 30 focused tests passed. Conformance passed all 7 tests after the golden update. Clippy passed for `camcraft-post` and `camcraft-app`, all targets, with warnings denied.

Quick gate: RED. It ran 648 steps. The failed-step rerun passed conformance. Only `continuous_4axis_part::the_continuous_4axis_part_posts_its_wrapped_program` remains red: `/version: 71 != 70`. This failure was reported before these changes. No unrelated fixture changed.

Needs changes before merge.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The PR changes posted G-code.

Earlier findings 1 and 3 are met. The post cancels cycles before travel and seats the next hole at the section hop. The tests cover missing hops and cycles after probing, feeds, and arcs. The vendor is now `Camcraft`. The earlier probe status and offset fixes remain present. Their tests pass.

### Requested before merge

1. **Supply the required simulator evidence** — `docs/decisions/2573-hurco-winmax-post.md:63`. Earlier finding 2 remains open. [Issue #2573](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/2573) requires one short program for each open dialect question in the owner's WinMax simulator. Record each successful load and the comparison with the CamCraft path on that issue. The decision file and PR body confirm that these results are absent. Changing the PR footer to `Refs #2573` does not meet this requirement. Local tests do not replace the simulator checks.
2. **Resolve the merge conflict when the PR is eligible for refresh** — `crates/post/tests/cycle_hop.rs:35`. The trial merge with current upstream main conflicts in the gate-map comment and `CYCLE_POSTS`. Main adds `linuxcnc.cps`; this PR adds `hurco-winmax.cps`. Retain both entries and update the array length. Run the cycle-hop suite on the merged result. Follow the project rule to refresh at merge time.

### Local validation

I used upstream main's current project laws at `4dddc38725387d0e3a3c67e87a7a6938329f5c89`.

The trial merge failed in `crates/post/tests/cycle_hop.rs`. I aborted it without resolving source conflicts. The results below apply to the PR head, not to a merged tree. All commands ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-2646`. No GitHub runner ran.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --no-run -j 6`: passed.
- Post suites passed: `hurco_winmax_post` 8, `hurco_winmax_probe` 2, `hurco_winmax_metadata` 1, `script_hurco_winmax` 11, `cycle_hop` 8, `bore_cycle` 9, `comp_plane` 3, `decimal_point_fanuc_family` 3, `declared_options` 3, `end_units` 3, `first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family` 9, `radius_arcs` 7.
- App suites passed: `hurco_winmax_post` 2, `conformance` 7, `machine` 33, `machine_library` 11, `post_spindle_rule_all` 5.
- Total: 125 tests passed. None failed or were ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -j 6 -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Independent mutation: bypassed `cycleSeat(p)`. Four cycle-hop tests failed. The failures covered low traverses and missing-hop refusals. Restored the call: all 8 tests passed.
- Independent mutation: removed `seatKnown = true` from `onLinear()`. `a_cycle_read_after_probing_or_cutting_is_seated_at_the_hop` failed. It detected travel at Z1 below the Z3 hop. Restored the assignment: the test passed.
- Both mutations were restored. No code change remains.
- I read all 21 NC goldens and four refusal goldens line by line. The synthesized golden now cancels cycles and raises to the hop before travel. No existing golden changes.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run`: passed; it selected 648 steps. I ran the touched suites directly. I did not run the full quick gate or reproduce the reported `continuous_4axis_part` example-version failure.

No UI, dependency, or process files change in this PR. No WinMax simulator or physical machine ran. The PR remains a draft.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
